tolerance.set_from: CPU calibration 4.98e-4 (worst of single_inputs 2.93e-4, single 1.21e-4, pair 4.98e-4) doubled; the margin covers chunk/fusion choices only, since CPU XLA has no autotune noise. 1e-3 also sits just above upstream's own cuEq-vs-Triton distance on this same capture (single 1.00e-4, pair 7.03e-4), whose coordinate counterpart is 0.0336 A -- below the panel's 0.05 A pass line.

entries.notes: Tier A compares the trunk boundary, which has no Angstrom: `tolerance.metric` is max|port-native| divided by max|native| per array, worst of the three, and `gpu_residual_angstrom` carries the panel's COORDINATE residual (port cuEq vs native cuEq, entity maxima per sample) because no GPU port run kept its trunk arrays -- the two that requested them (openbind-private-batched-20260909-QK9YSM, openbind-source-backend-20260909-A3bJ4y) no longer hold prediction.npz. Detection floor: measured on the stored native pair, upstream's own cuEq->Triton kernel swap moves the trunk by 7.03e-4 (pair) and the coordinates by 0.0336 A; scaling that ratio linearly, a trunk-origin defect big enough to break the 0.05 A pass band lands near 1.0e-3, which is this tolerance. The scaling is inference, not a measurement, so Angstrom-level detection is tier B's job. `capture.commit` and the `upstream_commit` tripwire are the upstream OpenBind commit because the capture is a native upstream run; there is no provenance.json in this capture root, so `capture.provenance` names its trace.json, which carries the same native_source commit and the trunk-array digest. `model_config.json` is the capture's `predictions/model_config.json` (the fixture layout is flat); the fetch helper matches by digest and finds it. The tape is a 609-key torch RNG call log and cannot be sliced to fewer samples or steps -- `load_capture` admits only the released n5/200-step/four-pass shape -- so both tiers replay the whole recorded schedule. Tripwire ladder actually run (each rung flips MSA one-hot categories on rows the tape selects for cycle 0, and reports its distance from the clean CPU run as proof the perturbed value reached the compiled program): 1 row x 1 token moves pair 1.53e-5 and does not trip; 1 row x 118 tokens moves it 1.00e-4 and does not trip; 16 rows moves it 1.13e-3 and trips (residual 1.27e-3 > 1.0e-3); 1024 rows moves it 1.61e-2 and trips 16x over. So the measured floor is between one and sixteen of 1024 MSA rows -- a single MSA cell is below it. single_inputs never moves in any rung, which is correct: the input embedder does not read the MSA.

tolerance.set_from: CPU calibration 0.0323 A (entity P, sample 4 -- the worst sample this entry asserts on) plus the native cuEq process floor 0.0147 A measured on this capture's own repeat = 0.047, rounded to the master panel's 0.05 A pass line.

entries.notes: Per-entity RMSD under one whole-system Kabsch fit per sample, entities grouped by chain_id -- bench.entity_parity.compare_entity_parity called with the arguments bench/openbind_core_report.py:compare calls it with. CPU calibration, all five samples: P [0.0144, 0.0157, 0.0676, 0.0216, 0.0323], R [0.0156, 0.0235, 0.0195, 0.0292, 0.0219]. Sample 2 is excluded: it is the amplifying sample of this capture on every stored pairing -- native cuEq vs its own repeat 0.0147 A, upstream's own cuEq vs Triton 0.0336 A, the GPU port vs native cuEq 0.0416 A (the panel's max, and its pass verdict), and this CPU replay 0.0676 A. Asserting it would force the whole entry to about 0.09 A and stop the four quiet samples from catching anything inside the pass band. Detection floor with sample 2 excluded: a regression has to add about 0.018 A to the worst kept sample (P sample 4, 0.0323 A) or about 0.035 A to the quietest (P sample 0, 0.0144 A). The tape cannot be sliced to fewer samples or steps (609-key torch RNG call log; load_capture admits only the released n5/200-step/four-pass shape), so this replays the whole recorded schedule; it costs 113.5 s on 8 pinned cores, compile included. Tripwire ladder actually run: flipping the sign of one initial-noise draw (000008_randn_torch_float32[0,0,0,0], 0.5237 -> -0.5237) fires -- the coordinates move 1.9e-5 A from the clean CPU run -- but does not trip, because the first denoising step at sigma_max discards a single atom's starting position. Flipping 16 selected MSA rows moves individual atoms up to 1.26 A and still does not trip (worst kept sample 0.0323 A): an RMSD over ~1,200 atoms averages a localized displacement away, which is a property of the panel's own metric, not of this entry. Flipping all 1,024 selected rows trips on every kept sample (P 0.0525/0.1720/0.1746/0.1164 A). What this entry detects is systematic displacement at the scale the panel scores, not a single-atom move.
